subquestion: R10 fresh-server small-batch RAW UUID TimeSeries SAMPLES 3600 vs 10800s write and merge
scientific_scope: Same binary and 400-slot 3d fixture, fresh-process 4-phase ABBA. The 10800s physical layout lowers explicit merge CPU/time; write CPU effect small relative to control variation. Not sustained production ingest+read workload.
compiler: LLVM 22.1.8 unmodified ClickHouse stock O1 with glibc lab allocator

method.isolation: Fresh ClickHouse watchdog/server process before each phase, one new RAW UUID v11 TimeSeries table, same runner and binary; background merges suspended while inserting; explicit START MERGES then OPTIMIZE FINAL on SAMPLES,TAGS,TimeRanges; STOP MERGES barrier before physical readback.
method.workload: 73 single-client sequential HTTP INSERTs per phase: 72 batches x400 series and final batch96 series; 28,896 series, 2,488,320 sample array elements; each 400-series batch contains 15s/60s/300s cadences.
method.process_cpu: Linux /proc/<server_pid>/stat user+system jiffies for all worker threads; measured ingest and explicit merge windows separately. QueryFinish ProfileEvents covers only part of async ingestion work.
method.partlog: system.part_log MergeParts six per phase after explicit optimize; ProfileEvents.OSCPUVirtualTimeMicroseconds aggregated across physical target merges.
method.correctness: Full nonempty native PromQL label/time/value parity across all 4 tables, 24 node-broad points and 3 namespace points per table; exact 2,488,320 point sum(length(samples)), expected 28,896 TAGS and TimeRanges rows, SAMPLES bucket rows 86,688 or 28,896 by step, all three inner targets one active part after optimize.
method.controls: A/B/B/A on same runner; baseline and candidate A/A drift under 25% for CPU, wall, disk; no rejected controls or OOM.
method.rss: Single low-cost process RSS monitor every 250ms; process restarted between phases; RSS observations are diagnostic, not proof of lower memory.
method.read_latency: Only one oracle query after each load; not a valid read-latency benchmark and not included in write/merge timing.

limits: Glbic O1 lab binary and a small synthetic 3d workload; not production jemalloc or real HPA/tenant traffic.
Background merges were stopped during INSERT and explicitly triggered after ingestion: steady-state merge scheduling and foreground read impact were not tested.
INSTRUMENTATION: /proc process CPU includes CPU work outside ingestion and merge (e.g. logs), but each phase is isolated in a fresh process. It is not isolated per query.
Difference in total ingest CPU is 4.4% with 2.52% baseline and 2.63% candidate drift; do not claim universal ingest speedup.
Merge process CPU 0.825->0.720s (-12.7%) and partlog MergeParts CPU mean ~681.7->586.8ms (-13.9%) corroborate direction on this specific load. More repetitions/real-data distributions are needed.
RSS observations 405MB,429MB,444MB,443MB are monotonic across phase order; not causal by variant.
Read timing and p95/p99 under concurrent remote-write and query workloads remain untested.
next_action: Extend R10 with steady-state writer and concurrent native PromQL reader at 1 and 4 clients, same 3600 vs 10800s variants and independent baseline/no-write control. Require full physical/native parity and p95/p99, total process CPU, RSS, generated/merged bytes, no broad OOM. Avoid overlapping R02 owner's existing write-path campaign.
